description: Cannabis Village at DEF CON 26 covers security, compliance, and technology in the cannabis industry. The talks explore cannabis software security breaches, regulatory compliance, genetic engineering, computer vision applications, hydroponic systems, and the intersection of cybersecurity and the emerging cannabis sector.

talks.title: Compliance and Infosec Within the Cannabis Industry
talks.teaser: Compliance and Infosec Within the Cannabis Industry
talks.summary:
### Cyber Risk in the Regulated Cannabis Sector
At 00:00, Alex Heid (speaking as "weed anon") introduces the technical security posture and unique compliance requirements facing the newly legalized commercial cannabis sector, an emerging industry characterized by rapid capitalization and immature infosec controls.

### Supply Chain Exposures and Interconnected Systems
At 05:00, Heid draws parallels between cannabis enterprise vulnerabilities and landmark corporate breaches like Target and OPM. Third-party vendor integration, shared HVAC management networks, and unsegmented corporate links provide external attackers with direct conduits into sensitive business operations.

### Exposed Perimeters and IoT Footprints
At 10:00, the speaker presents empirical reconnaissance data gathered using Shodan and Censys. Scans across regional cannabis operators reveal exposed seed-to-sale databases, unauthenticated administrative web interfaces, and point-of-sale (POS) systems directly accessible from the public internet.

### Flaws in Mandated Video Surveillance Infrastructure
At 15:00, Heid highlights severe vulnerabilities in physical security equipment. State regulations require licensed dispensaries and grow facilities to operate continuous video surveillance; however, facilities routinely deploy cheap, white-labeled OEM IP cameras that expose unauthenticated RTSP video streams and default credentials.

### Bridging Statutory Compliance and Real Defense
Concluding at 20:00, Heid emphasizes that meeting statutory state reporting requirements (such as METRC track-and-trace mandates) does not equate to effective security. Operators must implement foundational network segmentation, credential rotation, and supply-chain risk modeling to safeguard customer data and critical infrastructure.

talks.title: An Overview of Hydroponic Grow Techniques
talks.teaser: An Overview of Hydroponic Grow Techniques
talks.summary:
### Fundamentals of Hydroponic Engineering
At 00:00, Alex Bebek and Adrian Logan deliver a comprehensive engineering guide to hydroponic cultivation systems, breaking down the mechanics of soil-less agricultural infrastructure.

### Architectural Typologies of Hydroponic Systems
At 08:01, the presenters contrast primary hydroponic designs, including Deep Water Culture (DWC), Nutrient Film Technique (NFT), aeroponic misters, and closed-loop drip systems. They evaluate water reservoir sizing, oxygenation pump duty cycles, and root-zone mechanics across each implementation.

### Water Chemistry, Recirculation, and Nutrient Control
At 16:00, the discussion turns to aquatic chemistry management. Maintaining recirculating systems requires precise monitoring of electrical conductivity (EC), parts-per-million (PPM) mineral concentrations, water temperature, and automated pH balancing to prevent root rot pathogens and optimize nutrient uptake.

### Nutrient Balancing Across Crop Growth Stages
At 24:00, Bebek and Logan examine nutrient recipes, detailing shifts in nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium (NPK) ratios as crops transition from vegetative growth to flowering stages, explaining how micro-nutrient deficiencies manifest physically in leaf tissue.

### Sanitization Protocols and Automation Controls
Concluding between 32:00 and 40:01, the speakers review operational hygiene and automation. They explain sterilization procedures using ozone and food-grade hydrogen peroxide between harvest cycles, followed by a discussion of automated IoT controllers and sensor arrays deployed to monitor environmental metrics for regulatory and yield tracking.
